profile.name: Beth Mooney
profile.writeup:
Beth Mooney isn't one for the spotlight. She's the kind of cricketer who prefers to let her bat do the talking, quietly and consistently dismantling opposition bowling attacks. Yet, her achievements speak volumes, etching her name as one of the finest batters in women's cricket. From her early days filling in for her brother's team to becoming the first Australian woman to score centuries in all three international formats, Mooney's journey has been filled with perseverance and unwavering dedication, backed by undeniable statistics.


She comes from Victoria, and her sporting prowess was evident from a young age. She dabbled in everything from soccer to tennis and Australian rules football, but it was cricket that truly captured her heart. A serendipitous invitation to fill in for her brother's team ignited a passion that would shape her life. When her family moved to Hervey Bay, Queensland, her father became her first coach, their early morning bike rides and sea kayaking adventures fostering a strong bond.


Mooney's rise through the ranks was steady. She honed her skills playing for Hervey Bay's boys' team, facing the challenges of rural cricket where girls' teams were scarce. Her talent was undeniable, and by her teenage years, whispers of her potential to play for Australia began to circulate. She juggled her cricket dreams with a teaching degree, but in 2014, she made a defining decision to dedicate herself fully to cricket.


Her domestic career blossomed, and she made her debut for Queensland at just 16. One of her defining performances came in the WBBL 04 final in January 2019, when she battled illness and heat exhaustion to score 65 off 46 balls, helping Brisbane Heat secure their maiden title. She later moved to Western Australia and joined Perth Scorchers, where her remarkable consistency continued. During the following season, she became the first player to score 3,000 runs in WBBL history, underlining her standing as one of the competition's most dependable batters


Mooney's impact extended beyond Australian shores. In the inaugural Women's T20 League, she was a prized acquisition for Gujarat, bought for a staggering INR 2 crores. Despite an injury-ridden start, her return in subsequent seasons showcased her class, with a series of stellar performances, including 285 runs in 8 innings in 2024. In 2025, she scored 237 runs in 9 matches. Her consistency was a highlight for Gujarat. Her international career has been marked by consistency across formats and an ability to deliver on major occasions. From her T20I debut against India to her maiden Test century against England, Mooney has continued to expand her game.


In February 2025, she scored an unbeaten 106 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, becoming the first Australian woman to register centuries in all three international formats. The innings helped Australia retain the Ashes. Later that year, she produced a crucial century against Pakistan at the ODI World Cup, rescuing Australia from a difficult position in an otherwise relatively quiet campaign. She has also been part of Australia's successful campaigns at ICC tournaments and the 2022 Commonwealth Games, where the team won gold.


At the 2025 ODI World Cup, Beth endured a relatively quiet tournament by her high standards, managing just one century, which came when Australia were staring down the barrel against Pakistan. Following the World Cup, the Women’s T20 League retentions were announced, with Mooney among the two players Gujarat chose to retain ahead of the 2026 auction. During the 2025 Women Ashes series, she scored her maiden Test century against England to help Australia win the match and retain the trophy. She also continued to score heavily in the WPL, recording the most runs for the Gujarat Giants in the 2026 season.


She produced another defining chapter at the 2026 T20 World Cup in England. After a mixed start to the tournament, Mooney peaked when it mattered most. In the final against England at Lord's on 5 July, she scored 64 off 49 balls, anchoring Australia's chase of 151. Australia reached the target with seven wickets and 17 balls to spare, completing an unbeaten campaign and claiming their 7th Women's T20 World Cup title. Mooney was named both Player of the Match in the final and Player of the Tournament, finishing the competition with 238 runs from 7 matches.
